lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Independent application A: independence stated in conditional terms

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One reference example. Use it only if you get stuck.

items.prompt: 30 people; 18 do A, 14 do B, 7 do both. Find P(A or B).

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: An event has probability 3/7 on a single trial. Two independent trials are run. Find the probability of at least one success, as a fraction in lowest terms.
A survey table records: group X with 11 successes and 16 failures; group Y with 14 successes and 24 failures. Find P(success | group X) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Two events have P(A) = 1/10, P(B) = 9/10, and P(A and B) = 10/100. Are A and B independent?
choices: No; P(A and B) differs from P(A)·P(B).
No; the two events are mutually exclusive.
Yes; the two events cannot occur together.
Yes; P(A and B) equals P(A)·P(B).
